{"id": "33da8aabe6e16f93a795", "title": "Anthropic says it’s committing 5% of its shares to a ‘public benefit fund’", "url": "https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/18/anthropic-says-its-committing-5-of-its-shares-to-a-public-benefit-fund", "source_id": "techcrunch", "source": "TechCrunch AI", "published_at": "2026-10-18T20:37:40+00:00", "first_published_at": "2026-10-18T20:37:40+00:00", "announced_at": null, "updated_at": "2026-10-18T20:37:45+00:00", "feed_entry_at": "2026-10-18T20:37:40+00:00", "time_basis": "source_published", "text": "In Brief Posted: 1:37 PM PDT · October 18, 2026 Image Credits: Jakub Porzycki / NurPhoto / Getty Images Anthony Ha Anthropic says it’s committing 5% of its shares to a ‘public benefit fund’ Anthropic announced today that it’s creating a “public benefit fund” that will give the company “increased flexibility and scale” to support projects for societal good. Anthropic said that it will commit 5% of its shares to the fund — structured as a wholly-owned entity within the company — with the option to contribute an additional 2% for every 50% increase in Anthropic’s value. And it offered some broad-strokes ideas for how this money might actually be used, such as “large donations to traditional nonprofits or direct distributions to specific populations.” There’s also the impact that AI might have on the job market, which Anthropic has already committed $200 million to study . But the company said, “Given the pace of AI progress, bolder approaches may be needed. The Fund will have the versatility to pursue them.” Anthropic’s announcement comes as the AI industry faces increasingly negative public sentiment, which CEO Dario Amodei has described as “fundamentally a crisis of trust.” If you’re wondering who will actually decide which public benefits are worth funding, Anthropic said it will share more information about structure and governance in the coming months. {"id": "71e1590c6c971a337879", "title": "Disney agrees to hire the majority of Character.AI’s workforce", "url": "https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/18/disney-agrees-to-hire-the-majority-of-character-ais-workforce", "source_id": "techcrunch", "source": "TechCrunch AI", "published_at": "2026-10-18T16:30:00+00:00", "first_published_at": "2026-10-18T16:30:00+00:00", "announced_at": null, "updated_at": "2026-10-18T19:01:55+00:00", "feed_entry_at": "2026-10-18T16:30:00+00:00", "time_basis": "source_published", "text": "In Brief Posted: 9:30 AM PDT · October 18, 2026 Image Credits: Character.AI Anthony Ha Disney agrees to hire the majority of Character.AI’s workforce After chatbot startup Character.AI filed for bankruptcy earlier this week, many of its employees will have the opportunity to take jobs at Disney. Character.AI’s former CEO Karandeep Anand recently became the entertainment giant’s first CTO , and the startup previously said that Disney had agreed to acquire some of its assets for $20 million. A legal filing spotted by Bloomberg revealed more details about the agreement between Character.AI and Disney, with Disney agreeing to make employment offers to at least 60 Character.AI employees — the majority of the workforce — paying them an estimated $60 million in annual compensation. The filing also says that the “vast majority” of Character.AI employees who were offered jobs at Disney accepted them. However, this is a stalking horse bid, so another company could come forward with a higher offer. The filing says that despite its “large and engaged user base,” Character.AI has been hobbled by high costs and “potential litigation-related liabilities and regulatory engagement.” (The company was sued by the mother of a 14-year-old boy who said her son became obsessed with one of Character.AI’s chatbots before committing suicide; it also faces government investigations over child safety concerns .) {"id": "da92b80397690dde35e8", "title": "Structured Authority Injection: Persistent Human Control for LLM Agents via Typed MCP Overrides", "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22373", "source_id": "arxiv", "source": "arXiv cs.AI / cs.LG", "published_at": "2026-07-27T03:38:01+00:00", "first_published_at": "2026-07-27T03:38:01+00:00", "announced_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "updated_at": null, "feed_entry_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "time_basis": "feed_announcement", "text": "Abstract: LLM-based agents are increasingly used as autonomous orchestrators in distributed and multi-agent systems, yet a control gap remains: no protocol-level mechanism allows human operators to inject binding directives that persist across planning cycles. Free-text overrides suffer from ambiguous interpretation due to lack of schema validation and from authority erosion as operator instructions lose influence within accumulating context. We propose Structured Authority Injection (SAI), a protocol that addresses these issues by routing operator corrections through typed, schema-validated Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool calls and maintaining a ranked authority context prepended to each LLM prompt. SAI defines three override classes (Constraint, Priority, and Strategy) with distinct persistence semantics and an explicit precedence order enforced via a directed authority channel inaccessible to the planning process. The method requires no model fine-tuning or access to model weights and applies to instruction-tuned LLMs supporting MCP tool use. Evaluation across nine LLMs and eight scenarios targeting agent failure modes shows reduced ambiguous directive interpretation and mitigated authority decay across planning iterations, with lower prompt overhead in the strongest models (up to 38% depending on model and scenario), though benefit varies substantially across models. SAI provides a general design pattern for agent systems requiring explicit and persistent human control.", "evidence_kind": "abstract", "demo": false, "publication_kind": "preprint"}

{"id": "f34ad45741b405ff9e69", "title": "Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution", "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22466", "source_id": "arxiv", "source": "arXiv cs.AI / cs.LG", "published_at": "2026-10-15T17:39:38+00:00", "first_published_at": "2026-10-15T17:39:38+00:00", "announced_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "updated_at": null, "feed_entry_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "time_basis": "feed_announcement", "text": "Abstract: Harness evolution automatically optimizes the prompts, skills, tools, and orchestration code around a fixed-weight model, offering a way to improve agentic systems without updating model weights. The agent harness is iteratively optimized to achieve higher performance on the search set. But how much of this gain reflects benchmark-specific overfitting or additional inference-time compute, and how much may generalize beyond the search set? In this work, we introduce Harness-Delta Attribution (HDA), an evaluation protocol that dissects an evolution gain into artifact-driven overfitting, gains explained by test-time scaling, and the remainder, which gives an upper bound on residual generalizable improvement. We apply HDA to 11 executor models and three harness-evolution frameworks across math, coding, creativity, and agentic tasks. In 21 of these settings that show statistically significant search-set gains, we find that a large share of the improvement is explained by overfitting or test-time scaling. Specifically, among these 21 settings, overfitting and test-time scaling account for 54% and 14% of the gain on average; their combined share exceeds 50% in 14 settings. The residual and held-out transfer vary substantially across tasks, models, and frameworks. Importantly, search-set gains often fail to transfer to held-out tasks, and provide limited evidence that they will persist under practical distribution shifts. Moreover, validation-based signals are insufficient to prevent overfitting. These results motivate attribution-aware evaluation in future harness evolution research.", "evidence_kind": "abstract", "demo": false, "publication_kind": "preprint"}

{"id": "a97c1f5a709e4de6f7ba", "title": "Lean4AgenticRL: Advancing Agentic RL with Verifiable Multi-level Process Rewards", "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22448", "source_id": "arxiv", "source": "arXiv cs.AI / cs.LG", "published_at": "2026-10-15T15:26:54+00:00", "first_published_at": "2026-10-15T15:26:54+00:00", "announced_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "updated_at": null, "feed_entry_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "time_basis": "feed_announcement", "text": "Abstract: Enhancing the agentic capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) to tackle complex software engineering (SWE) and general terminal-usage problems is a pressing challenge. Current state-of-the-art LLMs often go through large-scale agentic Reinforcement Learning (RL). However, they mostly rely on high-level outcome rewards, with minimal consideration of low-level toolcall and mid-level workflow-stage rewards, which makes the training less effective. To overcome this limitation, we propose **Lean4AgenticRL**, which, to the best of our knowledge, is the first framework that grounds multi-level process rewards in the unified Lean4 formalization schema for open-ended agentic RL. **Lean4AgenticRL** first builds a *problem-specific workflow* system that balances the agent's own capability and controllability during execution, laying the foundation for further verification. Subsequently, our workflow formalization and multi-level reward annotation methods enable agent behavior verification within a general harness system. It provides multi-level rewards to support more effective agentic RL with the workflow-stage-normalized GRPO algorithm. Using **Lean4AgenticRL**, we train **LAR-9B/27B**, a family of models with enhanced agentic capability. Extensive experiments indicate that our model outperforms the leading model of similar size. **LAR-27B** achieves **77.3%** on TerminalBench-2.1. On average, our models outperform the base model by **9.89%** and surpass the second-best model of comparable size we know by **5.07%**. These results indicate the potential of integrating formal methods in enhancing open-ended agentic RL.", "evidence_kind": "abstract", "demo": false, "publication_kind": "preprint"}

{"id": "6ec636eceffcfb5999d5", "title": "Don't Retrain, Remix: Adaptation of Web Agents using Mixture Hypernetworks", "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22539", "source_id": "arxiv", "source": "arXiv cs.AI / cs.LG", "published_at": "2026-10-15T18:37:41+00:00", "first_published_at": "2026-10-15T18:37:41+00:00", "announced_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "updated_at": null, "feed_entry_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "time_basis": "feed_announcement", "text": "Abstract: The web is not static or uniform. Websites that serve the same purpose can look and navigate very differently. Even within a single site, successive redesigns can change how familiar features are presented and accessed. Humans adapt to this by recognizing familiar interaction patterns and reusing what they already know. We give web agents a similar ability with WebMix, a mixture hypernetwork that adapts them to unseen interfaces by composing previously trained low-rank adapters. WebMix begins with a bank of adapters trained on source interfaces. At deployment, a scout agent explores the target interface and summarizes its observations into a compact manual. A lightweight router uses this manual to predict mixing coefficients over the adapter bank, which combine the existing adapters into a new one for inference. Adapting to a new interface takes only a scouting run and a forward pass, without gradient updates on the target. With Qwen and Llama models, we evaluate domain transfer on TimeWarp and WebArena-Lite-v2, and version transfer on TimeWarp. In all three settings, WebMix matches or outperforms in-context learning and LoRA baselines, often matching the average success of specialists trained directly on those interfaces. On TimeWarp domain transfer, it gains about 8 percentage points on average over the best baseline with both models. These gains do not come at the cost of seen interfaces, where WebMix keeps its lead, and extend to version transfer. Adapting to a new interface can therefore rely on exploration and composition instead of retraining.", "evidence_kind": "abstract", "demo": false, "publication_kind": "preprint"}

{"id": "434246a93fec15537b14", "title": "PRIME: Towards Verifiable Evidence-Grounded Reasoning in LLM Agents", "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22426", "source_id": "arxiv", "source": "arXiv cs.AI / cs.LG", "published_at": "2026-10-15T05:03:22+00:00", "first_published_at": "2026-10-15T05:03:22+00:00", "announced_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "updated_at": null, "feed_entry_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "time_basis": "feed_announcement", "text": "Abstract: LLM agents are used to check records against an organization's requirements, for example whether a vulnerability report is ready for investigation. Requirements often allow several ways to be met, such as a severity rating with a curator-reviewed advisory or a published advisory link. Agents fail by accepting a report after a required check has failed, or by settling for a weaker conclusion without trying another way that could still succeed. We introduce PRIME (Precommitted Rules for Inference from Minimal Evidence). Before checking, it fixes evidence routes specifying how each conclusion may be justified. A separate program records each check result and refuses any conclusion the results do not justify. It also points the agent to checks that could justify a stronger conclusion, or runs them itself. PRIME reports only conclusions authorized by its rules and ledger. With correct requirements, exact checks at known locations, and sufficient budget at stopping, completion reaches the strongest supported conclusion. On 480 public-record tasks, an agent shown the requirements reported unjustified conclusions on 26.7% of tasks, while PRIME reported none. Its directions and added checks raised the average score for justified conclusions from 30.1, with refusal alone, to the maximum of 59.2 out of 100.", "evidence_kind": "abstract", "demo": false, "publication_kind": "preprint"}

{"id": "dd5a28f9c533e0ee2ccc", "title": "Trust but Verify: Designing Region-Inhomogeneous Forward Dynamics for Discrete Diffusion", "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22380", "source_id": "arxiv", "source": "arXiv cs.AI / cs.LG", "published_at": "2026-10-02T15:14:44+00:00", "first_published_at": "2026-10-02T15:14:44+00:00", "announced_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "updated_at": null, "feed_entry_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "time_basis": "feed_announcement", "text": "Abstract: Continuous diffusion treats the forward process as a design space; discrete language diffusion often uses absorbing corruption, leaving context fully trusted throughout generation. This makes trust binary: corrupted context is copied as ground truth, propagating errors into generated spans. We reopen this design space by combining absorbing and uniform-mixing kernels with region-dependent rates. Missing positions follow absorbing dynamics, while context undergoes low-rate random substitution, exposing the model to observed but uncertain tokens during training. At inference, a heuristic sampler re-injects noise into suspicious context under an annealed intensity and freezes context updates late in the trajectory. An 8,000-step finetune of a pretrained 170M-parameter masked diffusion model takes under five hours on a 6 GB laptop GPU. The base model assigns roughly 50% probability to observed tokens even when they are uniform-random garbage. For uniform-random corruption, finetuning detects corrupted context with 0.96 recall and 0.91 precision, improves infill token-F1 by 3.8 points at 10% corruption and 6.4 points at 20%, and removes the accuracy dip next to corruptions. Clean conditioning shows no measurable regression, with a false-edit rate below 0.4%. Gains for plausible corruptions are weaker: about 0.5 F1 points at 10% corruption, without statistical significance. Our results suggest that detectability and damage depend jointly on departure from the data conditional: nearby noise is hard to detect and semantically mild, while distant noise is conspicuous and destructive. We interpret absorbing diffusion as the infinite-contrast limit of a trust axis, analogous to the signal-to-noise gap between known and unknown regions in diffusion inpainting. In our setting of a 170M model and a single text domain, intermediate trust is reached by changing forward dynamics rather than architecture.", "evidence_kind": "abstract", "demo": false, "publication_kind": "preprint"}

arguments.title: AI 简报｜Agent 工具调用与编码模型（2026-10-19）
arguments.overview: 覆盖说明：OpenAI、Google AI、Hugging Face 三个 RSS 在过去 24 小时均返回 0 条；TechCrunch 仅两条（Anthropic 股权公益基金、迪士尼接收 Character.AI 多数员工），属融资/并构与人事类，与你的订阅主题不符且触及排除词，未收录。本期内容全部来自 arXiv 今日公告列表中与 Agent 工程、工具调用、编码/终端模型相关的预印本；它们均为较早首次提交的论文，只是今天进入公告，不视为今天新发表。arXiv 摘要多为作者自评，数值均按原文标注条件。
selections: article_id='da92b80397690dde35e8' summary='论文提出 Structured Authority Injection（SAI）：把人类操作者的修正指令改为带类型、经 schema 校验的 MCP 工具调用下发，并在每次提示前附加一份带排序的 authority context；覆盖分三类（Constraint、Priority、Strategy），各有持久化语义和明确优先级，通过规划过程无法访问的定向通道执行。方法不需要微调或权重访问，适用于支持 MCP 工具调用的指令微调模型。作者在 9 个 LLM、8 个针对 agent 失败模式的场景上评估，称减少了指令歧义解释并缓解了多轮规划中的“权限衰减”，最强模型上提示开销最多降低 38%（依模型与场景而异），但收益跨模型差异很大；摘要未给出绝对成功率。该文 7 月 27 日首次提交，今天进入 arXiv 公告。' why_it_matters='与你的“工具调用”关键词直接对口：如果你在做 agent 编排层，可以把人工干预（限流、优先级、策略变更）设计成 schema 化的 MCP 工具调用而不是塞进自由文本提示，并用独立通道保证优先级不被上下文稀释。' topic='Agent / 工具调用' relevance=3

article_id='f34ad45741b405ff9e69' summary='Harness-Delta Attribution（HDA）提出一种评估协议，把“harness 演化”（自动优化固定权重模型周围的提示、技能、工具与编排代码）带来的提升拆成三部分：基准特定过拟合、可由测试时算力扩展解释的部分，以及可作为可泛化提升上界的残差。作者对 11 个执行模型、3 个 harness 演化框架，在数学、编码、创造性和 agentic 任务上做了测试；在 21 个搜索集上提升统计显著的设置中，过拟合平均解释 54%、测试时扩展解释 14%，二者合计份额在 14 个设置中超过 50%。搜索集上的收益往往不能迁移到 held-out 任务，且仅靠验证集信号不足以阻止过拟合。该文 10 月 15 日首次提交，今天进入公告。' why_it_matters='你调 prompt、工具和编排代码时看到的分数上涨，很可能一半以上来自过拟合与更多推理算力；这套拆分方法可直接用于你的内部评测设计，避免把搜索集收益当成上线后的真实提升。' topic='AI 编程 / Agent 评测' relevance=3

article_id='a97c1f5a709e4de6f7ba' summary='Lean4AgenticRL 把 agentic RL 的多层过程奖励统一到 Lean4 形式化 schema 下：先构建问题特定的 workflow 系统，再对工具调用级（低层）与 workflow 阶段级（中层）行为做可验证奖励标注，配合 workflow-stage-normalized GRPO 训练。作者据此训练 LAR-9B/27B，官方称 LAR-27B 在 TerminalBench-2.1 上达到 77.3%，家族平均比基座模型高 9.89%，比其所知的同规模第二名模型高 5.07%。论文面向软件工程与终端操作任务；摘要未说明模型权重是否公开。该文 10 月 15 日首次提交，今天进入公告。' why_it_matters='如果你在为编码/终端 agent 选型或自训，这是一条关于“小参数模型 + 过程奖励”的路线参考；但 77.3% 是 TerminalBench-2.1 上的单一基准成绩，且为作者自评，不能当作通用能力结论。' topic='AI 编程 / Agent' relevance=3

article_id='434246a93fec15537b14' summary='PRIME 针对 LLM agent 做合规/记录核查时“漏检后仍下结论”的问题：在检查前先固定证据路径，规定每个结论可如何被证明；另用一个独立程序记录每次检查结果，拒绝记录不足以支撑的结论，并提示或自动执行能支撑更强结论的检查。在 480 个公共记录任务上，直接看需求的 agent 在 26.7% 的任务上给出未获证据支持的结论，PRIME 为 0；把“仅拒绝”的平均分 30.1（满分 59.2 口径见原文，100 分制）提升到 59.2。作者明确给出前提条件：需求描述正确、检查位置精确已知、停止时预算充足。该文 10 月 15 日首次提交，今天进入公告。' why_it_matters='这是把“结论必须由可审计的检查记录授权”工程化的一个样本，适合参考到后端 agent 的权限与审计设计里：把判定逻辑放在模型之外，只接受 ledger 支持的输出。' topic='Agent 可靠性' relevance=2

article_id='6ec636eceffcfb5999d5' summary='WebMix 用混合超网络让 web agent 适配未见界面：先用源界面训练一组低秩适配器；部署时由 scout agent 探索目标站点并写成一份紧凑“手册”，轻量 router 据此预测适配器混合系数，合成新适配器用于推理，全过程不在目标接口上做梯度更新。用 Qwen 与 Llama 模型在 TimeWarp 与 WebArena-Lite-v2 上做域迁移、并在 TimeWarp 上做版本迁移，三个设置中均匹配或超过 in-context learning 与 LoRA 基线；TimeWarp 域迁移上平均比最佳基线高约 8 个百分点，且未牺牲已见接口的表现。该文 10 月 15 日首次提交，今天进入公告。' why_it_matters='对需要把同一套 agent 部署到多个内部系统/频繁改版的场景，这是“探索 + 组合适配器”替代重训的思路；不过评测限于两个 web benchmark 与两个开源模型族，落地前需自测。' topic='Agent / 部署' relevance=2

items.title: PRIME: Towards Verifiable Evidence-Grounded Reasoning in LLM Agents
items.summary: PRIME 针对 LLM agent 做合规/记录核查时“漏检后仍下结论”的问题：在检查前先固定证据路径，规定每个结论可如何被证明；另用一个独立程序记录每次检查结果，拒绝记录不足以支撑的结论，并提示或自动执行能支撑更强结论的检查。在 480 个公共记录任务上，直接看需求的 agent 在 26.7% 的任务上给出未获证据支持的结论，PRIME 为 0；把“仅拒绝”的平均分 30.1（满分 59.2 口径见原文，100 分制）提升到 59.2。作者明确给出前提条件：需求描述正确、检查位置精确已知、停止时预算充足。该文 10 月 15 日首次提交，今天进入公告。
items.why_it_matters: 这是把“结论必须由可审计的检查记录授权”工程化的一个样本，适合参考到后端 agent 的权限与审计设计里：把判定逻辑放在模型之外，只接受 ledger 支持的输出。

items.title: Don't Retrain, Remix: Adaptation of Web Agents using Mixture Hypernetworks
items.summary: WebMix 用混合超网络让 web agent 适配未见界面：先用源界面训练一组低秩适配器；部署时由 scout agent 探索目标站点并写成一份紧凑“手册”，轻量 router 据此预测适配器混合系数，合成新适配器用于推理，全过程不在目标接口上做梯度更新。用 Qwen 与 Llama 模型在 TimeWarp 与 WebArena-Lite-v2 上做域迁移、并在 TimeWarp 上做版本迁移，三个设置中均匹配或超过 in-context learning 与 LoRA 基线；TimeWarp 域迁移上平均比最佳基线高约 8 个百分点，且未牺牲已见接口的表现。该文 10 月 15 日首次提交，今天进入公告。
items.why_it_matters: 对需要把同一套 agent 部署到多个内部系统/频繁改版的场景，这是“探索 + 组合适配器”替代重训的思路；不过评测限于两个 web benchmark 与两个开源模型族，落地前需自测。
